raw_response:
I will still farm mostly the way that has kept my house steady. I have done this for 30 years, so I do not start from empty. I look at what gave me grain and what did not waste too much money. Around here, wheat and maize are the main living, and I have well water, so I will put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation and keep a smaller piece for cotton. Cotton takes more watching and more spraying, and with some people working outside, I do not want too much of it. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than see the crop go yellow and lose yield. So on wheat I will feed it heavier, because wheat eats fertilizer and water if I want a good head. On maize after wheat, I will also feed it enough so it does not stay thin after the summer rain starts. Cotton I will keep on a smaller block and manage tighter, because it can make money but it needs more medicine and more labor. I watch what the better growers nearby do, and I do close to that, then I adjust a little by what my own field did last year. If the stand looks weak, I will add a little more urea. If the crop looks good, I will not waste extra bags.
